title: Switching-Cost Power
hook: A lot of your customers aren't loyal. Leaving just sounds like a hassle.
statement: Customers stay when leaving costs them more than staying does.
explainer: Retraining, moving data, rebuilding integrations, losing history. That friction keeps people even when a better option shows up. Earn it by being deeply useful, not with penalties they'll escape at renewal.
sop: List everything a customer loses or redoes if they leave you.
Estimate the total Switching Cost in time and dollars.
Estimate the Annual Value they get from you.
Divide to get your Lock-In score.
Raise it by getting built into their workflow, not with punishing contracts.
equation_example: Switching Cost $6,000 ÷ Annual Value $2,000 = 3. Above 1 means leaving costs more than a year of value, so they stay. Below 1 means leaving is cheap, and they're only staying while they're happy.
question: Write down what it would actually cost your best customer, in time and money, to leave.
closing_statement: Useful lock-in is loyalty. Penalty lock-in comes due at renewal.
caption:
Principle Nº 349: Switching-Cost Power

A lot of your customers aren't loyal. Leaving just sounds like a hassle.

Customers stay when leaving costs them more than staying does.
